title: Tamsin and the Regiment
premise: Coral Okonkwo, a courier for the collapsing Republic of Vessany, arrives at the mountain town of Tamsin's Ford carrying coded dispatches meant to secure an alliance before the republic falls. When the seasonal bridge closes early, she is trapped among the townsfolk of the Regiment — a self-governing workshop community with its own quiet laws — and must decode her final message while deciding whether the town's independence is worth protecting from both the republic's agents and her own handlers. As winter deepens, Coral discovers the message she carries could save the town or doom it, and that her years of practiced silence have made her complicit in worse than she knew. In the end she burns the original dispatch, delivers a forged one that buys Tamsin's Ford its freedom, and chooses to stay — trading her invisibility for belonging at last.
about_author: Oscar Underhill is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the correspondence of failed states and small rebellions. He writes historical fiction about the people history files under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Last Road Out
chapters.summary: Coral crosses the high pass toward Tamsin's Ford with her dispatch case chained to her wrist. POV: Coral. Beat: wary competence masking exhaustion; she counts the days left in the season.

chapters.title: A Town That Keeps Its Own Books
chapters.summary: Coral reaches the town and meets the workshop council, including the formidable master joiner Odile Vant. POV: Coral. Beat: first contact; she performs the harmless traveler while noting every exit.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Early snows collapse the bridge timbers; the ferryman refuses the crossing until spring. POV: Coral. Beat: trap springs shut; panic beneath a calm face.

chapters.title: Which Silences Keep People Safe
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: fifteen years earlier, young Coral learns courier craft from her mentor Sef, including the rule never to be remembered. POV: Coral (past). Beat: origin of her invisibility.

chapters.title: The Regiment
chapters.summary: Odile offers Coral work in the workshop through winter; Coral accepts to stay near the council archives. POV: Coral. Beat: reluctant shelter; first warmth she doesn't trust.

chapters.title: Tamsin
chapters.summary: Coral meets Tamsin, Odile's apprentice daughter, sharp-tongued and curious about the stranger. POV: Tamsin. Beat: the town seen from inside; suspicion turning to fascination.

chapters.title: What the Case Contains
chapters.summary: Alone, Coral begins decoding the dispatches: instructions to buy the town's militia charter for the republic's war effort. POV: Coral. Beat: dread; the mission is not what she was told.

chapters.title: Council of Joiners
chapters.summary: The council debates winter rations; Coral observes how power works without crowns. POV: Tamsin. Beat: admiration for the town's order — and noticing who is never asked to speak.

chapters.title: A Letter from Sef
chapters.summary: A delayed letter reveals Sef died in the capital's purge; his last line warns her to trust no handler. POV: Coral. Beat: grief and betrayal; her chain to the republic loosens.

chapters.title: Hands in the Sawdust
chapters.summary: Coral works the bench beside Tamsin, learning joinery badly and being teased for it. POV: Tamsin. Beat: found family's first small kindnesses.

chapters.title: The Visitor from Downriver
chapters.summary: A republican agent, Merrick Hale, arrives before the freeze on the last ferry, hunting the courier. POV: Coral. Beat: hunter at the door; her double life tightens.

chapters.title: Invisible by Design
chapters.summary: Coral hides in plain sight as a widowed seamstress's cousin; Hale interviews the town. POV: Coral. Beat: terror managed through performance; old skills as cage.

chapters.title: The Charter Question
chapters.summary: Hale presents the republic's offer to the council: protection for their militia rolls. POV: Tamsin. Beat: the town's future becomes a bargaining chip; Odile stalls.

chapters.title: Night Work
chapters.summary: Coral decodes the second dispatch: if the town refuses, the republic will declare it in rebellion and let the enemy army take it. POV: Coral. Beat: moral vertigo; silence now means complicity.

chapters.title: Confession at the Kiln
chapters.summary: Coral half-confesses to Tamsin by the pottery kiln — enough truth to test loyalty. POV: Tamsin. Beat: risk of trust; the first honest words in fifteen years.

chapters.title: Odile's Ledger
chapters.summary: Odile shows Coral the town's secret ledger of debts owed by the republic itself. POV: Coral. Beat: revelation — the town has leverage; so does she.

chapters.title: Hale Makes Friends
chapters.summary: Hale courts the ambitious councilor Brann with promises of rank under the new regime. POV: Tamsin. Beat: corruption's soft entry; a neighbor turns informant.

chapters.title: The Frozen River
chapters.summary: The river freezes solid enough to walk — escape possible, but the dispatches would die with her. POV: Coral. Beat: temptation to run; she stays, surprising herself.

chapters.title: Midwinter Assembly
chapters.summary: The whole town votes on the charter; Coral watches democracy decide its own peril. POV: Tamsin. Beat: belonging felt from the gallery; the vote is deferred, dangerously.

chapters.title: What Hale Knows
chapters.summary: Hale corners Coral privately: he has known who she is since the ferry. POV: Coral. Beat: mask off; he offers her survival in exchange for the town's compliance.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: Coral weighs Hale's bargain against Sef's warning; flashback to a town she once abandoned to keep silent. POV: Coral. Beat: guilt crystallizes into resolve.

chapters.title: Brann's Error
chapters.summary: Brann copies council documents for Hale; Tamsin catches him and must choose whom to tell. POV: Tamsin. Beat: loyalty tested between law and justice.

chapters.title: The Workshop Stands
chapters.summary: Sabotage damages the workshop roof in a storm; the town rebuilds overnight. POV: Coral. Beat: communal power witnessed; she stops calculating exits.

chapters.title: Two Couriers
chapters.summary: Coral and Hale circle each other openly now, each claiming the other is the traitor. POV: Coral. Beat: cold war within warm walls; stakes named aloud.

chapters.title: Tamsin's Choice
chapters.summary: Tamsin tells the council everything, vouching for Coral against Brann's accusations. POV: Tamsin. Beat: the found family chooses her back; Coral weeps for the first time in years.

chapters.title: The Third Dispatch
chapters.summary: Coral decodes the final message: orders to burn the workshop and blame the enemy, erasing the town's claim. POV: Coral. Beat: horror peaks; the mission was arson all along.

chapters.title: Council in the Dark
chapters.summary: By lamplight, Coral lays everything before the council — her mission, the codes, the plan. POV: Coral. Beat: surrender of secrecy; the room holds its breath, then believes her.

chapters.title: Brann's Bargain
chapters.summary: Exposed, Brann flees to Hale; together they move up the timetable for the burning. POV: Tamsin. Beat: the enemy acts; spring feels impossibly far.

chapters.title: The Forgery
chapters.summary: With Odile and the archive-keeper, Coral forges a counter-dispatch ordering the town spared as a supply depot. POV: Coral. Beat: her skills turned home; craft as salvation.

chapters.title: Fire Watch
chapters.summary: The night Brann comes with pitch and torch; the town, forewarned, takes him alive without a drop of blood. POV: Tamsin. Beat: triumph of the town's way over the republic's.

chapters.title: Hale's Last Ferry
chapters.summary: Confronted with the forged orders and a united town, Hale departs downriver, defeated by paperwork and solidarity. POV: Coral. Beat: anticlimax as victory; power undone by its own bureaucracy.

chapters.title: What Brann Confessed
chapters.summary: Brann, broken, reveals the republic has already fallen; the war is over and no one won. POV: Coral. Beat: grief for a country that was already a ghost.

chapters.title: Burning the Case
chapters.summary: Coral burns the true dispatches on the kiln fire, ending her service to a dead state. POV: Coral. Beat: liberation through destruction; the chain finally off her wrist.

chapters.title: Spring Thaw
chapters.summary: Ice breaks on the river; the road out reopens, and Coral realizes she no longer wants it. POV: Tamsin. Beat: the choice made visible; staying as courage.

chapters.title: The Ledger Settled
chapters.summary: The council formally records Coral as a member of the Regiment, debts and all. POV: Coral. Beat: official belonging; her name entered in a book that will outlast empires.

chapters.title: Apprentice
chapters.summary: Odile takes Coral on as a proper apprentice; her hands finally learn the work. POV: Coral. Beat: humility rewarded; identity rebuilt from shavings and glue.

chapters.title: Letters Downriver
chapters.summary: News arrives of refugees from the fallen capital; the town prepares to take them in. POV: Tamsin. Beat: the circle of shelter widens; Coral helps build the bunks.

chapters.title: What Coral Teaches
chapters.summary: Coral begins teaching the town's children cipher and memory-craft, tools for surviving whatever comes next. POV: Coral. Beat: inheritance; the silences become gifts instead of wounds.

chapters.title: The Bridge Rebuilt
chapters.summary: The whole town raises the new bridge; Coral drives the final peg beside Tamsin and Odile. POV: Tamsin. Beat: climax resolved into creation; a road out that no longer tempts.

chapters.title: A Name in the Book
chapters.summary: Epilogue, one year on: Coral signs the ledger's new page as Coral Okonkwo Vant, courier no more. POV: Coral. Beat: quiet resolution — belonging chosen, kept, and written down.
